subject: Molecular Enzymology & Cellular Metabolism
syllabus_context: Unit II: Enzyme Kinetics and Catalytic Mechanisms. Substrate concentration vs initial velocity, steady-state approximation, derivation of the Michaelis-Menten equation, physical meaning of Km and kcat, Lineweaver-Burk double reciprocal plots, competitive, non-competitive, and uncompetitive inhibition, allosteric regulation.
declared_learning_objective: Derive the Michaelis-Menten rate equation under the Briggs-Haldane steady-state assumption, explain the biochemical meaning of Km and catalytic efficiency (kcat/Km), contrast competitive versus non-competitive inhibition using Lineweaver-Burk transformations, and analyze allosteric feedback inhibition.

recording_quality.known_observability_limitations: Kinetic derivations and Lineweaver-Burk double-reciprocal graphs drawn on whiteboard and explained verbally.
